text:
Timing: 0:30-1:40

MEMORY ANCHOR: Important decisions depend on quantities that are inferred indirectly.

SAY THIS:
Groundwater supplies drinking water, irrigation and economic activity, particularly in semi-arid regions where monitoring is limited. Yet the quantities needed for management are rarely observed directly. We need to know how long water has been underground, which locations are connected along flow paths, and which reactions control water quality. Environmental and nuclear tracers provide information about residence time. Hydraulic observations constrain flow direction and connectivity. Hydrochemistry records mixing and reaction. Each evidence stream is valuable, but each provides only a partial view. The scientific challenge is therefore not simply to fit each dataset. It is to determine which combined groundwater interpretation remains defensible when observations are sparse, heterogeneous and uncertain.

TRANSITION:
That background leads to the specific problem addressed by the thesis.

DELIVERY CUE: Use the sequence: management need, partial observations, hidden quantities, integration challenge.

AVOID SAYING: Do not imply that every study area contains all three evidence streams.

text:
Timing: 1:40-3:10

MEMORY ANCHOR: Coupled system, sparse evidence, separate workflows, conflicting stories.

SAY THIS:
The problem is that groundwater residence time, flow-path connectivity and chemical evolution describe the same physical aquifer, but they are commonly analysed as separate inverse problems. In data-limited aquifers, each problem is already non-unique. Several age distributions may fit the same tracer signal. Several directed networks may fit sparse hydraulic evidence. Several reaction pathways may reproduce the same chemistry. When the analyses are performed separately, uncertainty from one stage is often passed forward as fixed truth in the next. The result can be several individually plausible but mutually incompatible aquifer stories. Even worse, combining evidence can make uncertainty appear smaller while the interpretation becomes less accurate. What was needed was a framework that couples uncertain evidence, tests global compatibility, measures incremental information and reports when the problem remains non-identifiable.

TRANSITION:
The source of that problem becomes clearer when the three unknowns are considered together.

DELIVERY CUE: Use four verbal signposts: coupled system, sparse evidence, separate workflows, conflicting stories.

AVOID SAYING: Do not say conventional methods are wrong; say their separate use leaves cross-domain consistency untested.

text:
Timing: 3:10-4:10

MEMORY ANCHOR: Age, topology and chemistry constrain one another.

SAY THIS:
Age, topology and chemistry cannot be interpreted independently. Tracer evidence constrains plausible travel times and mixing. Topology determines which samples can reasonably be compared along a directed flow path. Chemistry constrains which reactions are plausible between connected locations. A sequential workflow often estimates one domain first and then treats that estimate as known. HydroSheaf instead treats the relations themselves as uncertain. It asks whether locally plausible tracer, hydraulic and chemical relations can be assembled into a globally compatible interpretation. If they cannot, the conflict should remain visible rather than being averaged away. This local-to-global question is the conceptual thread connecting all six objectives.

TRANSITION:
With that scientific gap established, I can state the overall aim.

The first three objectives establish the foundation. Timing: 7:45-8:55

MEMORY ANCHOR: The novelty is coupling plus falsification, not inventing the ingredients.

SAY THIS:
The individual scientific ingredients are established. This thesis does not claim to invent tracer dating, directed graphs, sheaf theory, PHREEQC, MODFLOW or MODPATH. The novelty is the way those foundations are made operational together for groundwater inference. HydroSheaf provides a groundwater-specific executable coupling, treats uncertainty and identifiability as outputs, uses adverse controls to detect false confidence, and applies locked claim-decision rules. Its significance is that integration becomes falsifiable. The framework can show that evidence is informative, redundant or harmful. It can also diagnose which field interpretations cannot be supported. That changes integration from an assumption into a scientific question.

TRANSITION:
I will now explain the methodology used to test that question.

Timing: 8:55-10:15

MEMORY ANCHOR: Each objective has its own evidence and failure test.

SAY THIS:
The methodology is a staged and adversarial evaluation design. The review first defines the gap and the boundaries of defensible claims. Formalisation represents the three evidence domains as uncertain relations. Component benchmarks test residence time, topology and reaction inference separately. Robustness experiments then perturb assumptions, remove measurements and introduce conflicting evidence. Integration experiments measure incremental value, redundancy and negative transfer. Finally, field transfer applies evidence-ceiling diagnostics to Ghanaian datasets. This sequence prevents a common error: using one successful experiment to support every claim about the framework. Each claim is matched to the strongest evidence that can actually test it.

Timing: 10:15-11:35

MEMORY ANCHOR: A weight scores a relation; an affine map transforms it and tests compatibility.

SAY THIS:
An ordinary weighted graph describes which nodes are connected and assigns a scalar strength to each edge. That is useful, but it does not specify how a state measured at one node should be translated into the state expected at another node. In the tested scalar-affine representation, each edge has a gain and offset. Different edges can therefore express different relations. HydroSheaf then asks whether these locally plausible transformations compose into a global section. Inconsistent cycles produce residuals that can localise conflict. The tested contribution is scalar affine representation and conflict localisation. The software can represent broader multivariate stalks, but multivariate vector-stalk performance was not validated in this thesis.

TRANSITION:
Because representation alone does not validate performance, claims were placed on an explicit evidence ladder.

The validation architecture has five levels. Unit and conversion checks establish that declared inputs are represented correctly. Reference emulation asks whether HydroSheaf can closely reproduce an established public workflow. Controlled known-truth benchmarks test recovery when the answer is planted externally. Field transfer asks what real observations can support when truth is unavailable. The missing highest level is a matched field dataset containing age tracers, repeated hydraulic observations, chemistry and independently measured connectivity. I also used locked tests. Development cases selected methods and decision rules. Held-out cases were opened once for confirmatory evaluation. This protects negative results from being tuned away, although the protocol was Git-locked rather than externally preregistered.

SAY THIS:
Objective one identified four recurring limitations. First, residence-time, connectivity and reaction models were commonly interpreted in separate workflows. Second, non-uniqueness was often treated as a nuisance rather than a primary result. Third, good observational fit was sometimes allowed to stand in for correct process identification. Fourth, additional evidence was frequently assumed to improve inference without an explicit incremental-value test. The literature therefore supplied mature component methods but not a complete solution to cross-domain compatibility. The discussion arising from the review is that the missing contribution was not simply another isolated model. It was a falsifiable way to test whether uncertain local relations remain mutually compatible when combined.

Timing: 16:20-18:10

MEMORY ANCHOR: Close reference agreement; no robust gain from the available graph proxy.

SAY THIS:
The public age archive contained 1,272 harmonised rows, of which 329 passed the strict reportability guard. Against the reported USGS and TracerLPM configurations, HydroSheaf achieved a median absolute log-ten age discrepancy of 0.0279, an R-squared of 0.937 and 87.5 percent agreement within a factor of two. This is close reference agreement, not formal equivalence and not independently observed age truth. The important integration stress test was whether topology added value. The weak hydraulic proxy changed RMSE by only minus 0.00135 and worsened factor-two agreement, so it failed the improvement rule. Wrong-direction and random graphs worsened RMSE substantially. HydroSheaf therefore reproduced the reported outputs closely and detected harmful topology, but it did not beat TracerLPM or establish useful graph information in that dataset.

Timing: 18:10-19:45

MEMORY ANCHOR: Topology inference was useful but conditional and imperfect.

SAY THIS:
For topology, MODPATH particle tracks supplied a model-conditioned reference network. Head-gradient inference achieved precision 0.49, recall 0.84 and F1 0.62, while negative controls were near zero. The relatively high recall shows that much of the directed structure was detected, but precision shows that false positives remained substantial. Independent scenarios also varied across evidence levels and spatial scales. It is essential to separate reference construction from unknown-graph inference. Conversion asks whether known particle paths are represented correctly. Inference asks whether an unknown graph can be reconstructed from indirect observations. The supported conclusion is conditional topology skill against MODPATH-derived reference transitions, not independently measured field connectivity.
